title: A generic free submodule with flat cokernel of smaller closed-fibre support
statement: Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a commutative local ring and $A\to B$ a flat finitely presented homomorphism [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map, def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. Assume every fibre is geometrically integral, meaning that $B\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak a)$ is a nonzero integral domain after every field extension of $\kappa(\mathfrak a)$ for every prime $\mathfrak a\subset A$. Suppose the closed fibre $\operatorname{Spec}(B/\mathfrak mB)$ has Krull dimension $n<\infty$ [def-kun-dimension]. Let $\mathfrak q\subset B$ lie over $\mathfrak m$ and let $N$ be a finite $B$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] with $N_{\mathfrak q}$ flat over $A$. Put $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak mB$. Then $\mathfrak p$ is prime and there exist $r\geq0$ and a $B$-linear map $\alpha:B^r\to N$ for which $\alpha\otimes_B\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is an isomorphism. The $r$ basis vectors may be sent to elements of any specified finite generating list of $N$; $r=0$ is allowed. For $Q=\operatorname{coker}\alpha$, the module $Q$ is finite, $\alpha$ is $A$-universally injective (for every $A$-module $L$, $L\otimes_A\alpha$ is injective), $Q_{\mathfrak q}$ is $A$-flat, and $0\to B^r\to N\to Q\to0$ remains exact after every base change of $A$. The support $\{\mathfrak r\in\operatorname{Spec}(B/\mathfrak mB):(Q/\mathfrak mQ)_{\mathfrak r}\ne0\}$ is a proper closed subset of the integral closed fibre and does not contain its generic point $\mathfrak p/\mathfrak mB$. If nonempty its Krull dimension is strictly less than $n$; in particular its dimension at $\mathfrak q$ is $<n$ whenever $\mathfrak q$ lies in it. If $n=0$ the support is empty. Localization, spectra, residue fields and tensor products mean [def-weil-pbc-module-localization, def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-residue-field, def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]; a cokernel here is the quotient $N/\operatorname{im}\alpha$.

proof.text: Put $C=B/\mathfrak mB$. Since $A$ is local, $C=B\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak m)$; the maps $b\otimes\bar a\mapsto\overline{ab}$ and $\bar b\mapsto b\otimes1$ are inverse. The fibre hypothesis makes $C$ a nonzero domain, so $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak mB$ is prime. Set $K=\kappa(\mathfrak p)=\operatorname{Frac}(C)$, using the residue-field definition and localization at $\mathfrak p$. The point $(0)$ of $\operatorname{Spec}C$ belongs to every nonempty basic open $D(c)$, since then $c\ne0$; it is the generic point and the closed fibre is irreducible.

source.place: Tag 05I3 (lemma-induction-step), choice of alpha and implication (1) to (2); Tag 05I5 (proposition-finite-type-flat-at-point), first proof, induction step

proof.text: Fix the specified generators $x_1,\ldots,x_t$ of $N$. Their images $x_i\otimes1$ span $V=N\otimes_B K$: expand the $N$ entry of each pure tensor in these generators. Scan this finite list, retaining a vector exactly when it is outside the span of those retained so far. The retained list is independent by construction and spans every scanned vector, hence is a basis of $V$. If it has length $r$, send the standard basis of $B^r$ to the corresponding $x_i$. This defines $\alpha$ and makes $\alpha\otimes_B K$ an isomorphism. If $V=0$, retain the empty list and use $r=0$.

source.place: Tag 05I3 (lemma-induction-step), choice of alpha and implication (1) to (2); Tag 05I5 (proposition-finite-type-flat-at-point), first proof, induction step

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-local-generic-basis-universal-injective] to $R=A$, $S=B$, $q=\mathfrak q$, $\xi=\mathfrak p$, and the map just chosen. The ring map is flat and finitely presented, all its fibres are geometrically integral, $\mathfrak q$ lies over the maximal ideal, $N$ is finite, $N_{\mathfrak q}$ is $A$-flat, and the generic residue-field map is an isomorphism. Thus $\alpha$ is $A$-universally injective and $Q_{\mathfrak q}$ is $A$-flat for $Q=N/\operatorname{im}\alpha$.

source.place: Tag 05I3 (lemma-induction-step), choice of alpha and implication (1) to (2); Tag 05I5 (proposition-finite-type-flat-at-point), first proof, induction step

proof.text: The images of $x_1,\ldots,x_t$ generate $Q$, so $Q$ is finite. Universal injectivity, evaluated on $L=A$, makes $\alpha$ injective. For every $A$-module $L$, tensor right exactness gives exactness at the last two terms of $L\otimes_A B^r\to L\otimes_A N\to L\otimes_A Q\to0$, and step 3 gives injectivity at the first term. In particular take $L=A\prime$ for any $A$-algebra $A\prime$: this proves the asserted short exact sequence after every base change.

source.place: Tag 05I3 (lemma-induction-step), choice of alpha and implication (1) to (2); Tag 05I5 (proposition-finite-type-flat-at-point), first proof, induction step

proof.text: Let $T=Q/\mathfrak mQ$, finite over $C$ via the same generators. Tensor the defining cokernel sequence with $K$ over $B$. Tensor right exactness and the isomorphism $\alpha\otimes_B K$ give $Q\otimes_B K=0$. This is $T_{(0)}$: explicitly $q\otimes(\bar b/\bar s)\mapsto\bar b\bar q/\bar s$, with inverse $\bar q/\bar s\mapsto q\otimes1/\bar s$, where $s\notin\mathfrak p$. The tensor relations kill $\mathfrak mQ$ and give well-defined mutually inverse maps. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-module-support-annihilator], $Z=\operatorname{Supp}_C(T)=V(\operatorname{Ann}_C(T))$ is closed. Since $T_{(0)}=0$, it misses the generic point, and hence is proper.

source.place: Tag 05I3 (lemma-induction-step), choice of alpha and implication (1) to (2); Tag 05I5 (proposition-finite-type-flat-at-point), first proof, induction step

proof.text: Apply [new-node-irreducible-open-complement-dimension] to the irreducible space $X=\operatorname{Spec}C$, $d=n$, and the nonempty open $U=X\setminus Z$. It gives either $Z=\varnothing$, or $\dim Z\le e<n$ for some natural number $e$. At a point of $Z$, its dimension is at most $\dim Z$: the whole $Z$ is one of the open neighbourhoods in the defining minimum. Thus the dimension at $\mathfrak q$ is $<n$ whenever $\mathfrak q/\mathfrak mB\in Z$. For $n=0$ the alternative $e<n$ is impossible, so $Z$ is empty.
